title: = I37a: Bundle II's extraction and acquisition, no laws: the verifier router (MultipleVersionRollupVerifier) extracted at the pinned head, modelled (model3's untyped machine with a storage-dynamic-array extension outside every generator closure) and linked with the adopted Rollup into one machine in which the Rollup's proof checks run the router and the router's finalization check reads the Rollup, refined against a forge harness of the real Rollup and router; the zkEVM verifier (ZkEvmVerifierV1 with its SP1 and Plonk bases), the circuit oracle of HypC, extracted only with its debt named; the public-input view and the cost sites read from the documents; acquisition notes from committed records and git objects, no network read

predictions.claim: The router is extracted as read (E1, E2): gen/M3/bundle2/documents/router.json exists and the declaration lists no debt for it; its coverage has no unaccounted statement and exactly one debt entry, the external_call IRollup.lastFinalizedBatchIndex at MultipleVersionRollupVerifier.sol:149 (thresholds.debt.router); its actions are the eight of thresholds.structure.router (five own, three of OpenZeppelin's Ownable 4.9: owner, renounceOwnership, transferOwnership), its own families rollup, legacyVerifiers and latestVerifier in that order with one inherited entry (_owner) and no constant; getVerifier and verifyAggregateProof (which inlines it) each have one loop record and one cost term, both the linear search at :108-114; verifyAggregateProof has the one COMMIT edge IZkEvmVerifier.verifyBatch. Derivation: reading the source under I19's rules: the verifyBatch call is a COMMIT edge (IZkEvmVerifier is the router's commit interface, as IRollupVerifier is the Rollup's), so the one call that is not is the Rollup getter's; the search loop reads storage and writes none, so it is a cost term, not debt; the constructor's loop is not an action; struct copies, member assignments on a memory struct, an index into a storage array of structs and a push are in the walk's term language (holon.frontends.solidity.transitions: member, index, len, push), so none of them is unsupported.

The zkEVM verifier is extracted with named debt (E1, E2): its extraction ends within the sidecar's budget (1800 s) with a document and no member debt; its actions are the eight of thresholds.structure.zkevm (verifyBatch and verifyPlonk; SP1Verifier's VERSION, VERIFIER_HASH, VK_ROOT, hashPublicValues and verifyProof; PlonkVerifier's Verify); its coverage has no unaccounted statement; its external_call debt is exactly the three external self calls this.verifyPlonk (ZkEvmVerifierV1.sol:23), this.verifyProof (:27) and this.Verify (SP1VerifierPlonk.sol:81); and its debt holds at least one unsupported entry in PlonkVerifier.sol (the Yul staticcalls to the SHA-256, ecAdd, ecMul, pairing and modexp precompiles are builtins the walk does not represent). Derivation: reading the sources under I19's rules; the Plonk check is the circuit, the oracle I37 states as HypC, so its debt is named here and never modelled. This is the least certain prediction: the walk has never run on 1100 lines of Yul with nested functions and loops, and an extraction error or a timeout misses it.

The declaration's static links (L2) are the four rows of thresholds.links: the Rollup's three proof checks (commitBatchWithProof, proveCommittedBatchState and proveState, the COMMIT call at Rollup.sol:779-784) into the router's action verifyAggregateProof, and the router's updateVerifier call at :149 into the Rollup's getter lastFinalizedBatchIndex; they are the instrument's rule over the committed documents. Derivation: the Rollup's three rows are rule L2 on the committed document (a disclosed construction fact; only their callee kind needs the router's document); the router's row is from reading (rollup is a storage family wired to the Rollup, which has no action of that name but a public family).

The linked machine refines the real Rollup and router (L1-L8, C1-C6): on the whole corpus, 300 m1, 5 seed and 60 random traces (thresholds.corpus_traces), every compared step agrees in status, revert key, return data, every member's storage at every touched slot, the members' logs and the frames: no disagreement, no unsupported step, and results/M3/bundle2/disagreements.json lists none. Derivation: I20 refined the Rollup's document with no disagreement on its corpus; the router's verifyAggregateProof is a view whose only external call goes to a stand-in (answered from the record), and its updateVerifier reads the Rollup through a getter while the Rollup is not on the stack, so no step re-enters a writing member (L5); the harness's stand-ins accept as I20's verifier stand-in did, so the m1 traces reach the Rollup's guards as in I20.

The corpus reaches every link and every router action, recounted by the instrument from the harness's frames (steps.json): each of the four link rows is executed with a persisted frame at least once (the m1 traces' proof-backed commits and proofs and the seed traces S2 and S3 for the Rollup rows; S1, S2 and S4 for the getter row), and each of the router's eight actions ends in a persisted frame at least once (initialize through S4 and S5's poked steps; renounceOwnership in S4). Derivation: the seed traces were planted past the guards as the sources read (the owner is the harness; batch 1 is committed with the genesis post root 100 and finalized after F + 1 seconds; the stand-in Z1 accepts proof byte 1, Z2 byte 2).

The router's model compiles and refines (M1-M3): gen/M3/bundle2/models/models.json lists the router with no model debt; the model holds no escape hatch and the pinned Bend prints ALL PROOFS CHECK on it (no law: a type and termination check); and on every compared top-level router step of the corpus, its compiled model (holon.sorts.evaluate3) agrees with the real router in status, revert key, storage writes and logs: no disagreement, no unsupported step. Derivation: model3 compiles the adopted Rollup's mappings, structs, packing, loops with break, custom errors and calls; what the router adds is storage dynamic arrays (an index into legacyVerifiers[v], its length and a push), which the prereg assigns to an additive extension under holon/bundle2/.

regressions.claim: Earlier extractions and models do not move (E3; green at the prereg): the inputs of thresholds.inputs_sha256 keep their sha256; the adopted Rollup document re-extracts byte for byte with its sidecar; holon coverage --milestone M2 --check and --milestone M3 --check pass; the typed and untyped M3 model texts (.bend) of the adopted document regenerate byte for byte (its init.json is written by holon run since F40, with a code table holon model does not write, so it is not compared).

I80's own commits (the contract's definition) change only what the contract allows: at least one adds gen/M3/bundle2/bundle2.json; none changes a frozen root, laws/, spec/, holon/rules/, holon/frontends/, a file of thresholds.closures (the generator closures at the prereg: 149 files), a file under replay/ outside replay/M3/bundle2/, a file under gen/ outside gen/M3/bundle2/, or a file under results/ outside results/M3/bundle2/. So no record is re-made and every committed record stays current.

holon audit prereg passes for M2 and M3 (tested). On CI, on the build head: gate-M0, gate-M1 and gate-M2 pass; gate-M3-partial and gate-M3-G2 fail only on the base's items (thresholds.base_gate_M3), its G3 scanning the router's model; tests-m3-catalog, the frozen suite, freeze-check and both audits pass. The full M3 gate is not claimed.
holon/bundle2/ (construction) exists, imports no test module, names no target contract, address or host, and no file of it is in any generator closure at HEAD.

thresholds.disclosed: Read before this prereg: the router's, ZkEvmVerifierV1's, SP1VerifierPlonk's and PlonkVerifier's sources and their interfaces at the head; Rollup.sol's _verifyProof, proof actions, commit and finalize logic; OpenZeppelin's Ownable 4.9; the adopted Rollup document's call records of IRollupVerifier.verifyAggregateProof (their receivers and argument terms: P3's Rollup rows and E4's view); I63's committed receipts (the anchor); the tag tree listings (no blob read but the head's units); the basis (the instrument's builds of the head units under I63's configurations). Run: the instrument's basis; a toy forge test of the state-diff 'reverted' flag (it is set for a frame whose enclosing frame reverted). Never run on a Bundle II member: the frontend, model3, the evaluator, forge or Bend.
